mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as funding costs decline across the economy.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 1.5% (25th percentile), or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals labor market deterioration, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when UNRATE rises >0.3pp, or Rank IC < 0.01 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate collapsing consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as earnings expectations fall.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles, rising FEDFUNDS compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, generating negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS >2.0% and rising, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: Higher industrial production (INDPRO) reflects robust manufacturing activity, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when INDPRO >105 (75th percentile), or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.3% signals accelerating inflation, triggering central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when CPIAUCSL monthly change >0.3%, or Rank IC < 0.01 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent weak employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate labor market deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days as recession risks intensify.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when PAYEMS growth <0.1% and UNRATE rises, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, declining housing starts (HOUST) signal weakening consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as economic peaks approach.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when UNRATE <4.0% and GDPC1 growth >2.0% (q/q) and HOUST declines, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3 years.
